body:
Reviewed the full 131-page immutable diff (86 files, head `5c44cd7b`) — canonical relationship writers, inter-process reservation, dependency admission, source-preserving frontmatter morphisms, CLI/HTTP/MCP error classification — reading every changed hunk plus the complete surrounding source of each touched module.

**Deterministic evidence:** exact-head clean checkout, all 10 hosted gates exit 0 (lint 0/0, test 245/2261/0 twice, four release builds 0 warnings, release outputs), errors []. Committed RED logs in the diff are historical TDD captures, not current failures.

**Confirmed findings (2, both non-blocking, documentation contract):**
1. `docs/verification/relationship-writer.md:49` — the PR-introduced checkpoint's present-tense §Implementation says conflict/partial kinds "retain the existing internal exit-code fallback of4", but head maps `:conflict 3` (cli.cljs:40), this PR's own docs/cli.md rows say 3, `exit-codes-are-stable` pins it, and the PR's retained process proof records `code: 3`. The doc corrects itself 140 lines later (lines 190-192, 207) but scopes that correction to the earlier proof, leaving two incompatible current-behavior statements about a contractual value. Fix line 49 to 3/4.
2. `src/rheos/backend/infra/cli.cljs:190` (exposing `docs/cli.md:157-161`) — this PR widens `frontmatter` to `parent`/`epic`/`dependency` (task_edit now runs `relationships/admit-update`; CLI help, MCP schema/description and HTTP handler all updated; the PR's own test asserts those edits succeed) but the CLI reference still claims frontmatter "writes only the closed mutable set" of descriptive keys. Every other surface was updated; docs/cli.md was edited in this PR for the exit rows but this enumeration was missed. An agent reading only that doc may hand-edit cards outside the new reservation/ledger writer.

**Rejected under adversarial validation:** flow-style multi-pair line removal data loss (flow mappings are refused by `source-document`, so accepted pairs are one per line); kindless YAML-validation exit paths (same guard runs at load, so unreachable after a successful load); MCP `minProperties 1` empty-updates (matches HTTP's existing 400); widened `(merge result ...)` dropping `:kind` on refusals (`refusal`/`move-task!` always attach it, so FSM refusals still exit 3).

**Non-blocking notes:** `create --epic`/`--dependency` are absent from docs/cli.md, but that doc delegates flag lists to `rheos help <verb>` and the help registry carries them; no inline test-gap findings — new admission/reservation/partial-effect branches are covered by `relationship_admission_test.cljs` and `law/dependency_admission_test.cljs`, with the compiled CLI/HTTP/MCP parity matrix explicitly deferred to the successor parity story.
